gloss: myriad; eight million; innumerable (especially of gods)

definitions.explanation: An extremely large, uncountable number. Most famously used in the Shinto concept of {八百万|やおよろず}の{神|かみ} (eight million gods / myriad deities), expressing the belief that divine spirits reside in all things.

examples.japanese: {八百万|やおよろず}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{神|かみ}→神：02147_kami⟧。

examples.english: It is said that there are eight million gods in Japan.

examples.japanese: {八百万|やおよろず}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{神|かみ}→神：02147_kami⟧⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{考|かんが}え{方|かた}→考え方：10169_kangaekata⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦あらゆる→あらゆる：03824_arayuru⟧もの⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{神|かみ}→神：02147_kami⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{宿|やど}る→宿る：12351_yadoru⟧⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{信仰|しんこう}→信仰：03685_shinkou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{基|もと}づいている→基づく：02315_motozuku⟧。
examples.english: The concept of myriad gods is based on the belief that divine spirits dwell in all things in nature.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {八百万|やおよろず}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{神|かみ}→神：02147_kami⟧ (the myriad gods, the eight million deities)

USAGE:
Almost exclusively used in the expression {八百万|やおよろず}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{神|かみ}→神：02147_kami⟧, a core concept in Shinto. The number "eight million" is not literal but represents an inconceivably large number — the idea that gods and spirits inhabit everything in the natural world: mountains, rivers, trees, rocks, and even everyday objects. This concept is foundational to Japanese animism and is often cited to explain Japan's polytheistic religious worldview. The reading やおよろず is an old Japanese number reading ({八百|やお} = 800, {万|よろず} = 10,000).
